records.source: Προσέχετε δὲ τὴν δικαιοσύνην ὑμῶν μὴ ποιεῖν ἔμπροσθεν τῶν ἀνθρώπων πρὸς τὸ θεαθῆναι αὐτοῖς· εἰ δὲ μή γε, μισθὸν οὐκ ἔχετε παρὰ τῷ πατρὶ ὑμῶν τῷ ἐν τοῖς οὐρανοῖς.
records.gloss: Beware then the righteousness of you not to do before the men in order to be seen by them; if but not indeed, reward not you have with the Father of you the in the heavens.
pieces: Take care not to put your righteousness on show for others to see. If you do, your Father in heaven has no reward for you.

L.1: But be careful not to do your righteousness before {{gender:people|men}} in order to be seen by them; otherwise you have no reward with your Father who [is] in the heavens.

R.1: Be careful! When you do what is righteous, do not do it in front of people just so they will see you. If you do, you will get no reward from your Father in heaven.

decisions.choice: righteousness: acts of devotion to God
decisions.reason: Here righteousness is the practice of piety. The three examples follow: giving to the poor (6:2-4), prayer (6:5-15) and fasting (6:16-18).

decisions.choice: in order to be seen by them: the purpose is the problem, not being seen
alternatives: never doing good where others can see
decisions.reason: Jesus has told his disciples to let their good deeds be seen so that God is glorified (5:16). What he forbids is doing them for one's own praise.

decisions.choice: righteousness, the reading of the SBLGNT
alternatives: alms, the reading of many later manuscripts
decisions.reason: Many later manuscripts have "alms" here, the word of 6:2. Early manuscripts have "righteousness". Reviewers should check the evidence against the apparatus.

records.heading: Not for show

records.source: Ὅταν οὖν ποιῇς ἐλεημοσύνην, μὴ σαλπίσῃς ἔμπροσθέν σου, ὥσπερ οἱ ὑποκριταὶ ποιοῦσιν ἐν ταῖς συναγωγαῖς καὶ ἐν ταῖς ῥύμαις, ὅπως δοξασθῶσιν ὑπὸ τῶν ἀνθρώπων· ἀμὴν λέγω ὑμῖν, ἀπέχουσιν τὸν μισθὸν αὐτῶν.
records.gloss: When therefore you do alms, not sound a trumpet before you, as the hypocrites do in the synagogues and in the streets, so that they may be glorified by the men; truly I say to you, they have the reward of them.
pieces: So when you give to the poor, do not announce it with trumpets, as the hypocrites do in the synagogues and on the streets to win praise from others. Truly I tell you, they have already been paid in full.

L.2: So when you give alms, do not sound a trumpet before you, as the hypocrites do in the synagogues and in the streets, so that they may be glorified by {{gender:people|men}}. Truly I tell you, they have their reward in full.

R.2: So when you give money to people in need, do not make a big show of it. The hypocrites do that in the synagogues and on the streets, so that people will praise them. I tell you the truth, the praise they get is all the reward they will ever have.

decisions.choice: alms: gifts to the poor
decisions.reason: Giving to the poor was a central duty of Jewish piety (Deuteronomy 15:11; Tobit 12:8).

decisions.choice: do not sound a trumpet: do not draw attention to your giving
alternatives: a literal trumpet blown at the time of giving
decisions.reason: No source shows that trumpets were blown when alms were given. The phrase is a picture of self-advertisement.

decisions.choice: hypocrites: people who act a part, whose piety is a performance
decisions.reason: The word first meant a stage actor. Jesus uses it of those whose religious acts are done for an audience (6:2, 5, 16; 23:13-29).

decisions.choice: be glorified: be praised by people
decisions.reason: The verb usually speaks of giving glory to God. Here it is the praise of people, which is what the hypocrites seek.

decisions.choice: they have their reward: they have been paid in full, and there is nothing more
decisions.reason: The verb was used on receipts: "received in full". The praise of people is the whole of their reward.

decisions.choice: win praise (B); praise them (R)
decisions.reason: The key term "glorify" is used of honor given to God. Here the honor is human, so Balanced and Readable say "praise", as the meaning note explains.

records.source: σοῦ δὲ ποιοῦντος ἐλεημοσύνην μὴ γνώτω ἡ ἀριστερά σου τί ποιεῖ ἡ δεξιά σου, ὅπως ᾖ σου ἡ ἐλεημοσύνη ἐν τῷ κρυπτῷ· καὶ ὁ πατήρ σου ὁ βλέπων ἐν τῷ κρυπτῷ ἀποδώσει σοι.
records.gloss: Of you then doing alms not let know the left of you what does the right of you, \v 4 so that may be your the alms in the secret; and the Father of you the seeing in the secret will repay you.
pieces: But when you give, keep it so quiet that your left hand does not know what your right hand is doing.
Your gift will be hidden, and your Father, who sees what is hidden, will repay you.

L.3: But when you give alms, do not let your left [hand] know what your right is doing,
L.4: so that your alms may be in secret; and your Father who sees in secret will reward you.

R.3: But when you give to someone in need, do it so quietly that even your left hand does not know what your right hand is doing.
R.4: Give in secret. Your Father sees what you do in secret, and {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} will reward you.

decisions.choice: left hand, right hand: give without fuss, without even dwelling on it yourself
alternatives: keep it from your closest friend
decisions.reason: The overstatement says the giving should be so quiet that it is hidden even from oneself.

decisions.choice: your Father who sees in secret will reward you: God sees and gives what he has promised
alternatives: a wage earned by the act
decisions.reason: What is done for God alone is seen by him. The reward is his gift, in this life and at the last day (6:20; 25:34-40).

decisions.choice: will reward you, the reading of the SBLGNT
alternatives: will reward you openly, the reading of many later manuscripts
decisions.reason: Many later manuscripts add "openly" here and in 6:6 and 6:18. Early manuscripts lack it. Reviewers should check the evidence against the apparatus.

records.source: Καὶ ὅταν προσεύχησθε, οὐκ ἔσεσθε ὡς οἱ ὑποκριταί· ὅτι φιλοῦσιν ἐν ταῖς συναγωγαῖς καὶ ἐν ταῖς γωνίαις τῶν πλατειῶν ἑστῶτες προσεύχεσθαι, ὅπως φανῶσιν τοῖς ἀνθρώποις· ἀμὴν λέγω ὑμῖν, ἀπέχουσι τὸν μισθὸν αὐτῶν.
records.gloss: And when you pray, not you will be as the hypocrites; for they love in the synagogues and in the corners of the wide streets standing to pray, so that they may be seen by the men; truly I say to you, they have the reward of them.
pieces: And when you pray, do not be like the hypocrites. They love to stand and pray in the synagogues and at the street corners where others can see them. Truly I tell you, they have been paid in full.

L.5: And when you pray, you shall not be like the hypocrites, for they love to stand and pray in the synagogues and on the corners of the wide streets, so that they may be seen by {{gender:people|men}}. Truly I tell you, they have their reward in full.

R.5: When you pray, do not be like the hypocrites. They love to stand up and pray in the synagogues and on street corners, so that people will see them. I tell you the truth, that is all the reward they will get.

decisions.choice: standing to pray at the street corners: praying where the most people pass
alternatives: a rule that prayer must be in private
decisions.reason: Jews stood to pray, at set hours of the day. Someone who was out when the hour came could stop where he was; the hypocrites make sure that is at a busy corner.

decisions.choice: hypocrites: people who act a part, whose piety is a performance
decisions.reason: The word first meant a stage actor. Jesus uses it of those whose religious acts are done for an audience (6:2, 5, 16; 23:13-29).

decisions.choice: they have their reward: they have been paid in full, and there is nothing more
decisions.reason: The verb was used on receipts: "received in full". The praise of people is the whole of their reward.

records.heading: Prayer

records.source: σὺ δὲ ὅταν προσεύχῃ, εἴσελθε εἰς τὸ ταμεῖόν σου καὶ κλείσας τὴν θύραν σου πρόσευξαι τῷ πατρί σου τῷ ἐν τῷ κρυπτῷ· καὶ ὁ πατήρ σου ὁ βλέπων ἐν τῷ κρυπτῷ ἀποδώσει σοι.
records.gloss: You but when you pray, go into the inner room of you and having shut the door of you pray to the Father of you the in the secret; and the Father of you the seeing in the secret will repay you.
pieces: But when you pray, go into an inner room, shut the door, and pray to your Father who is there in secret. Your Father sees what is hidden, and {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} will repay you.

L.6: But you, when you pray, go into your inner room, and having shut your door, pray to your Father who [is] in secret; and your Father who sees in secret will reward you.

R.6: But when you pray, go into a room by yourself and shut the door. Pray to your Father. He is there with you, though no one can see {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}. Your Father sees what you do in secret, and {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} will reward you.

decisions.choice: inner room: a storeroom, the one room in a house with a door that shut
decisions.reason: Most houses had one main room; the storeroom was the place where one could be alone.

decisions.choice: you, singular: each one's own prayer
decisions.reason: The address changes to the singular. Jesus is not forbidding public prayer, which the Lord's Prayer itself assumes ("our Father"), but prayer made for show.

decisions.choice: your Father who sees in secret will reward you: God sees and gives what he has promised
alternatives: a wage earned by the act
decisions.reason: What is done for God alone is seen by him. The reward is his gift, in this life and at the last day (6:20; 25:34-40).

records.source: Προσευχόμενοι δὲ μὴ βατταλογήσητε ὥσπερ οἱ ἐθνικοί, δοκοῦσιν γὰρ ὅτι ἐν τῇ πολυλογίᾳ αὐτῶν εἰσακουσθήσονται·
records.gloss: Praying but not babble as the Gentiles, they think for that in the many words of them they will be heard;
pieces: When you pray, do not keep piling up empty words as the pagans do. They think they will be heard because they say so much.

L.7: And when praying, do not babble like the Gentiles, for they think that in their many words they will be heard.

R.7: When you pray, do not keep saying words that mean nothing, like people who do not know God. They think they will be heard if they use a lot of words.

decisions.choice: babble: pile up words without meaning
decisions.reason: The verb is rare and seems to imitate meaningless sounds. Pagan prayers often listed many names of gods and repeated formulas to make sure of being heard. Jesus himself prayed the same words more than once (26:44).

decisions.choice: the Gentiles: pagans, who did not know the God of Israel
decisions.reason: As in 5:47.

records.source: μὴ οὖν ὁμοιωθῆτε αὐτοῖς, οἶδεν γὰρ ὁ πατὴρ ὑμῶν ὧν χρείαν ἔχετε πρὸ τοῦ ὑμᾶς αἰτῆσαι αὐτόν.
records.gloss: Not therefore be like them, knows for the Father of you of what need you have before the you to ask him.
pieces: So do not imitate them. Your Father already knows what you need before you ask {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}.

L.8: So do not be like them, for your Father knows what you need before you ask {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}.

R.8: Do not be like them. Your Father knows what you need even before you ask {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}.

decisions.choice: your Father knows: prayer does not inform God or wear him down
alternatives: there is no need to pray
decisions.reason: Jesus still teaches his disciples to ask (6:9-13; 7:7-11). They pray as children to a Father who already cares, not to persuade a reluctant god.

records.source: Οὕτως οὖν προσεύχεσθε ὑμεῖς· Πάτερ ἡμῶν ὁ ἐν τοῖς οὐρανοῖς· ἁγιασθήτω τὸ ὄνομά σου, ἐλθέτω ἡ βασιλεία σου, γενηθήτω τὸ θέλημά σου, ὡς ἐν οὐρανῷ καὶ ἐπὶ γῆς·
records.gloss: Thus therefore pray you: Father of us the in the heavens, let be made holy the name of you; \v 10 let come the kingdom of you; let be done the will of you, as in heaven also on earth;
pieces: So this is how you should pray: 'Our Father in heaven, may {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} name be kept holy.
May {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} kingdom come. May {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} will be done on earth, as it is done in heaven.

L.9: So pray like this: 'Our Father who [is] in the heavens, let {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} name be made holy;
L.10: let {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} kingdom come; let {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} will be done, as in heaven, so also on earth;

R.9: So when you pray, pray like this: 'Our Father in heaven, may everyone honor {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} name as holy.
R.10: May {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} kingdom come. May people on earth do what {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} want, just as it is done in heaven.

decisions.choice: Our Father in heaven: God addressed with a child's trust and with reverence
decisions.reason: Jesus calls God Father and teaches his disciples to do the same. "In heaven" keeps his greatness in view.

decisions.choice: let your name be made holy: may God show his holiness, and may all honor it
alternatives: only a wish that people respect God
decisions.reason: God's name stands for God himself. The passive asks God to act so that his name is treated as holy (Ezekiel 36:23), and includes the honor his people give it.

decisions.choice: as in heaven, so on earth: may cover all three requests
alternatives: only the request about God's will
decisions.reason: The phrase follows the third request but may belong to all three: God's name, kingdom and will, honored on earth as in heaven.

decisions.choice: you: emphatic, you my disciples, unlike the pagans
decisions.reason: The pronoun is written out, setting the disciples' prayer against 6:7-8.

decisions.choice: your, you for God, with deity_pronoun spans
decisions.reason: The prayer speaks to God, so "your" and "you" take the usual span.

decisions.choice: may your name be kept holy (B); may everyone honor your name as holy (R)
decisions.reason: "Hallowed" is no longer current English. Balanced keeps the passive; Readable says who honors the name.

records.heading: The Lord's Prayer

records.source: τὸν ἄρτον ἡμῶν τὸν ἐπιούσιον δὸς ἡμῖν σήμερον·
records.gloss: The bread of us the daily give us today;
pieces: Give us today the bread we need.

L.11: Give us today our daily bread;

R.11: Give us the food we need for today.

decisions.choice: daily: the bread needed for this day or the coming one
alternatives: the bread we need to live
decisions.reason: The word is found almost nowhere outside the Lord's Prayer, and its meaning is uncertain. It may mean "for the coming day" or "needed for life". Either way the request is for what is needed now, as God gave manna day by day (Exodus 16:4).

decisions.choice: food
decisions.reason: Bread stands for food in general. Readable says so.

records.source: καὶ ἄφες ἡμῖν τὰ ὀφειλήματα ἡμῶν, ὡς καὶ ἡμεῖς ἀφήκαμεν τοῖς ὀφειλέταις ἡμῶν·
records.gloss: and forgive us the debts of us, as also we forgave the debtors of us;
pieces: Forgive us what we owe {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}, as we too have forgiven those who owe us.

L.12: and forgive us our debts, as we also have forgiven our debtors;

R.12: Forgive us for the wrong things we have done, as we have forgiven people who have done wrong to us.

decisions.choice: debts: sins, as what we owe God
decisions.reason: In Aramaic the word for debt was also used of sin. Luke has "sins" (Luke 11:4), and Jesus speaks of "trespasses" in 6:14-15.

decisions.choice: as we have forgiven: those who ask forgiveness have already forgiven others
alternatives: a payment that earns God's forgiveness
decisions.reason: The past tense says the one who prays has already let others off. 6:14-15 and the parable in 18:23-35 show that God's forgiveness makes forgivers of those who receive it.

decisions.choice: what we owe you, with a deity_pronoun span
decisions.reason: Balanced keeps the picture of debt and says to whom it is owed.

records.source: καὶ μὴ εἰσενέγκῃς ἡμᾶς εἰς πειρασμόν, ἀλλὰ ῥῦσαι ἡμᾶς ἀπὸ τοῦ πονηροῦ.
records.gloss: and not bring us into temptation, but rescue us from the evil.
pieces: And do not lead us into testing, but rescue us from the evil one.'

L.13: and do not bring us into temptation, but rescue us from the evil one.'

R.13: Do not bring us into times of testing. Save us from the evil one.'

decisions.choice: temptation: testing, a trial that could lead to falling away
decisions.reason: The word covers both a test of faith and an enticement to sin. God is not the one who tempts to sin (James 1:13); the request asks him to keep his children from trials they could not stand, as Jesus tells his disciples to pray in 26:41.

decisions.choice: the evil one: the devil
decisions.reason: As in 5:37, the form can be masculine or neuter. The tempter of 4:1-11 is the likely sense.

decisions.choice: the prayer ends here, the reading of the SBLGNT
alternatives: with "For yours is the kingdom and the power and the glory for ever. Amen." added, in many later manuscripts
decisions.reason: The closing words of praise are not in the earliest manuscripts. They were added in the church's use of the prayer, following a pattern like 1 Chronicles 29:11. Reviewers should check the evidence against the apparatus.

decisions.choice: testing (B); times of testing (R)
decisions.reason: "Temptation" in English means only enticement to sin. Balanced and Readable use the wider word; Literal keeps the traditional one.

records.source: ἐὰν γὰρ ἀφῆτε τοῖς ἀνθρώποις τὰ παραπτώματα αὐτῶν, ἀφήσει καὶ ὑμῖν ὁ πατὴρ ὑμῶν ὁ οὐράνιος·
records.gloss: If for you forgive the men the trespasses of them, will forgive also you the Father of you the heavenly;
pieces: For if you forgive others when they wrong you, your Father in heaven will forgive you as well.

L.14: For if you forgive {{gender:people|men}} their trespasses, your heavenly Father will also forgive you,

R.14: If you forgive people the wrong things they have done to you, your Father in heaven will forgive you too.

decisions.choice: trespasses: wrongs, false steps
decisions.reason: The word means a stepping aside from the right way. It explains the "debts" of 6:12.

decisions.choice: forgiving and being forgiven belong together
alternatives: God's forgiveness is earned by forgiving
decisions.reason: Jesus comments on one request of the prayer. Those who will not forgive show they have not received God's mercy (18:32-35).

records.source: ἐὰν δὲ μὴ ἀφῆτε τοῖς ἀνθρώποις, οὐδὲ ὁ πατὴρ ὑμῶν ἀφήσει τὰ παραπτώματα ὑμῶν.
records.gloss: if but not you forgive the men, neither the Father of you will forgive the trespasses of you.
pieces: But if you refuse to forgive others, your Father will not forgive your wrongs either.

L.15: but if you do not forgive {{gender:people|men}}, neither will your Father forgive your trespasses.

R.15: But if you do not forgive other people, your Father will not forgive the wrong things you have done.

decisions.choice: the negative half: a warning
decisions.reason: The two verses state the same truth from both sides, as Jewish teaching often did.

records.source: Ὅταν δὲ νηστεύητε, μὴ γίνεσθε ὡς οἱ ὑποκριταὶ σκυθρωποί, ἀφανίζουσιν γὰρ τὰ πρόσωπα αὐτῶν ὅπως φανῶσιν τοῖς ἀνθρώποις νηστεύοντες· ἀμὴν λέγω ὑμῖν, ἀπέχουσιν τὸν μισθὸν αὐτῶν.
records.gloss: When but you fast, not be as the hypocrites gloomy, they disfigure for the faces of them so that they may appear to the men fasting; truly I say to you, they have the reward of them.
pieces: When you fast, do not put on a sad face as the hypocrites do. They make their faces look gloomy so that others will see they are fasting. Truly I tell you, they have been paid in full.

L.16: And when you fast, do not be gloomy like the hypocrites, for they disfigure their faces so that they may appear to {{gender:people|men}} as fasting. Truly I tell you, they have their reward in full.

R.16: When you go without food to pray, do not look sad like the hypocrites. They make their faces look sad so people will know they are fasting. I tell you the truth, that is all the reward they will get.

decisions.choice: fast: go without food for a time, as an act of devotion
decisions.reason: The law required a fast on the Day of Atonement (Leviticus 16:29). Devout Jews also fasted on other days; the Pharisee in Luke 18:12 fasts twice a week.

decisions.choice: disfigure ... appear: they hide their faces so that they will be seen
decisions.reason: The two verbs make a play on words: they make their faces unseen (unwashed, uncombed, perhaps with ashes) in order to be seen fasting.

decisions.choice: hypocrites: people who act a part, whose piety is a performance
decisions.reason: The word first meant a stage actor. Jesus uses it of those whose religious acts are done for an audience (6:2, 5, 16; 23:13-29).

decisions.choice: they have their reward: they have been paid in full, and there is nothing more
decisions.reason: The verb was used on receipts: "received in full". The praise of people is the whole of their reward.

decisions.choice: go without food to pray
decisions.reason: Readable says what fasting is.

records.heading: Fasting

records.source: σὺ δὲ νηστεύων ἄλειψαί σου τὴν κεφαλὴν καὶ τὸ πρόσωπόν σου νίψαι, ὅπως μὴ φανῇς τοῖς ἀνθρώποις νηστεύων ἀλλὰ τῷ πατρί σου τῷ ἐν τῷ κρυφαίῳ· καὶ ὁ πατήρ σου ὁ βλέπων ἐν τῷ κρυφαίῳ ἀποδώσει σοι.
records.gloss: You but fasting anoint of you the head and the face of you wash, \v 18 so that not you may appear to the men fasting but to the Father of you the in the secret; and the Father of you the seeing in the secret will repay you.
pieces: But when you fast, put oil on your head and wash your face,
so that no one but your Father, who is there in secret, will know that you are fasting. Your Father sees what is hidden, and {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} will repay you.

L.17: But you, when you fast, anoint your head and wash your face,
L.18: so that you may not appear to {{gender:people|men}} as fasting, but to your Father who [is] in secret; and your Father who sees in secret will reward you.

R.17: But when you fast, take care of your hair and wash your face, as you do every day.
R.18: Then people will not know that you are fasting. Only your Father, who is with you in secret, will know. Your Father sees what you do in secret, and {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} will reward you.

decisions.choice: anoint your head and wash your face: groom yourself as on any ordinary day
decisions.reason: People put olive oil on their hair as part of daily grooming. The point is to look as usual, so that no one can tell.

decisions.choice: your Father who sees in secret will reward you: God sees and gives what he has promised
alternatives: a wage earned by the act
decisions.reason: What is done for God alone is seen by him. The reward is his gift, in this life and at the last day (6:20; 25:34-40).

decisions.choice: take care of your hair, as you do every day
decisions.reason: Anointing is unfamiliar as grooming; Readable says what it meant.

records.source: Μὴ θησαυρίζετε ὑμῖν θησαυροὺς ἐπὶ τῆς γῆς, ὅπου σὴς καὶ βρῶσις ἀφανίζει, καὶ ὅπου κλέπται διορύσσουσιν καὶ κλέπτουσιν·
records.gloss: Not store up for yourselves treasures on the earth, where moth and rust destroy, and where thieves dig through and steal;
pieces: Do not pile up treasures for yourselves on earth, where moths and rust ruin them and thieves dig through walls and steal them.

L.19: Do not store up for yourselves treasures on earth, where moth and rust destroy, and where thieves break in and steal,

R.19: Do not save up riches for yourselves here on earth. Moths and rust can destroy them, and robbers can break in and steal them.

decisions.choice: rust: corrosion, or the eating away of stored goods
decisions.reason: The word means "eating". It may be rust on metal, or pests eating stored food and cloth. Moths ate the fine clothes in which wealth was often kept.

decisions.choice: break in: dig through the wall
decisions.reason: Many houses had walls of mud brick, which a thief could dig through.

records.heading: Treasure in heaven

records.source: θησαυρίζετε δὲ ὑμῖν θησαυροὺς ἐν οὐρανῷ, ὅπου οὔτε σὴς οὔτε βρῶσις ἀφανίζει, καὶ ὅπου κλέπται οὐ διορύσσουσιν οὐδὲ κλέπτουσιν·
records.gloss: store up but for yourselves treasures in heaven, where neither moth nor rust destroys, and where thieves not dig through nor steal;
pieces: Instead, pile up treasures for yourselves in heaven, where no moth or rust can ruin them and no thief can dig through and steal.

L.20: but store up for yourselves treasures in heaven, where neither moth nor rust destroys, and where thieves do not break in or steal.

R.20: Instead, save up riches for yourselves in heaven. There, moths and rust cannot destroy them, and robbers cannot break in and steal them.

decisions.choice: treasures in heaven: what God keeps for those who give and obey
decisions.reason: Jesus tells the rich man to sell what he has and give to the poor, "and you will have treasure in heaven" (19:21). What is given away for God is kept by God.

records.source: ὅπου γάρ ἐστιν ὁ θησαυρός σου, ἐκεῖ ἔσται καὶ ἡ καρδία σου.
records.gloss: where for is the treasure of you, there will be also the heart of you.
pieces: Your heart will always be where your treasure is.

L.21: For where your treasure is, there your heart will be also.

R.21: Your heart will be wherever your riches are.

decisions.choice: heart: what a person loves and lives for
decisions.reason: The heart is the center of a person's will and devotion. What people value most draws their whole life after it.

decisions.choice: your: singular here, after the plural of 6:19-20
decisions.reason: The saying is put to each listener personally.

records.source: Ὁ λύχνος τοῦ σώματός ἐστιν ὁ ὀφθαλμός.
records.gloss: The lamp of the body is the eye.
pieces: The eye is the lamp of the body.

L.22: The lamp of the body is the eye.

R.22: Your eye is like a lamp for your body.

decisions.choice: the eye as a lamp: the way light reaches the whole person
decisions.reason: People spoke of the eye as letting light in, or as a lamp shining out. Jesus uses the picture for how a person looks at life and possessions.

records.source: ἐὰν οὖν ᾖ ὁ ὀφθαλμός σου ἁπλοῦς, ὅλον τὸ σῶμά σου φωτεινὸν ἔσται·
records.gloss: If therefore is the eye of you single, whole the body of you full of light will be;
pieces: So if your eye is sound, your whole body will be full of light.

L.22: So if your eye is healthy, your whole body will be full of light,

R.22: If your eyes are good, your whole body will be full of light.

decisions.choice: healthy: sound, single, and so generous
decisions.reason: The word means single or undivided, and was used of generosity. Between sayings about treasure (6:19-21) and money (6:24), a healthy eye is an undivided devotion that shows itself in generosity.

records.source: ἐὰν δὲ ὁ ὀφθαλμός σου πονηρὸς ᾖ, ὅλον τὸ σῶμά σου σκοτεινὸν ἔσται.
records.gloss: if but the eye of you evil is, whole the body of you full of darkness will be.
pieces: But if your eye is bad, your whole body will be full of darkness.

L.23: but if your eye is bad, your whole body will be full of darkness.

R.23: But if your eyes are bad, your whole body will be full of darkness.

decisions.choice: a bad eye: an evil eye, that is, a stingy and greedy spirit
decisions.reason: In Hebrew an "evil eye" means a grudging, greedy attitude (Deuteronomy 15:9; Proverbs 28:22), and Jesus uses the phrase that way in 20:15.

records.source: εἰ οὖν τὸ φῶς τὸ ἐν σοὶ σκότος ἐστίν, τὸ σκότος πόσον.
records.gloss: If therefore the light the in you darkness is, the darkness how great.
pieces: So if the light inside you is really darkness, how deep that darkness is!

L.23: If then the light that [is] in you is darkness, how great the darkness!

R.23: If the light inside you is really darkness, then you are in very great darkness.

decisions.choice: the light in you is darkness: the means of seeing has become blind
decisions.reason: If what should guide a person is itself corrupted by greed, there is nothing left to show the way.

records.source: Οὐδεὶς δύναται δυσὶ κυρίοις δουλεύειν· ἢ γὰρ τὸν ἕνα μισήσει καὶ τὸν ἕτερον ἀγαπήσει, ἢ ἑνὸς ἀνθέξεται καὶ τοῦ ἑτέρου καταφρονήσει.
records.gloss: No one is able two masters to serve; either for the one he will hate and the other he will love, or one he will hold to and the other he will despise.
pieces: No one can serve two masters. Either {{gender:they|he}} will hate one and love the other, or {{gender:they|he}} will be loyal to one and look down on the other.

L.24: No one can serve two masters, for either {{gender:they|he}} will hate the one and love the other, or {{gender:they|he}} will be devoted to one and despise the other.

R.24: No one can serve two masters at the same time. {{gender:They|He}} will hate one master and love the other, or {{gender:they|he}} will be loyal to one and not care about the other.

decisions.choice: serve: serve as a slave, who belongs wholly to a master
decisions.reason: The verb is the one used of slaves. A slave owned by two masters could not give both full service; Jesus uses the picture of total loyalty.

decisions.choice: hate ... love: prefer one and reject the other
decisions.reason: In Hebrew idiom "love" and "hate" can mean choosing one over the other (Genesis 29:30-31; Malachi 1:2-3).

decisions.choice: serve
decisions.reason: "Serve" in Balanced and Readable, as the style guide has it for the slave words; the meaning decision (m1) keeps that this is a slave's service to a master, and Literal says "serve" too.

records.source: οὐ δύνασθε θεῷ δουλεύειν καὶ μαμωνᾷ.
records.gloss: Not you are able God to serve and mammon.
pieces: You cannot serve both God and money.

L.24: You cannot serve God and mammon.

R.24: You cannot serve God and money at the same time.

decisions.choice: mammon: wealth and possessions, spoken of as a master
decisions.reason: Mammon is an Aramaic word for wealth or property. Jesus pictures it as a rival lord who claims a person's service.

decisions.choice: mammon (L); money (B, R)
decisions.reason: Literal keeps the Aramaic word. Balanced and Readable use the plain English word.

decisions.choice: serve
decisions.reason: "Serve" in Balanced and Readable, as the style guide has it for the slave words and as in the first half of 6:24, where the meaning decision says this is a slave's service to a master; Literal says "serve" too.

records.source: Διὰ τοῦτο λέγω ὑμῖν· μὴ μεριμνᾶτε τῇ ψυχῇ ὑμῶν τί φάγητε, μηδὲ τῷ σώματι ὑμῶν τί ἐνδύσησθε· οὐχὶ ἡ ψυχὴ πλεῖόν ἐστι τῆς τροφῆς καὶ τὸ σῶμα τοῦ ἐνδύματος;
records.gloss: Because of this I say to you, not be anxious [for] the life of you what you will eat, nor [for] the body of you what you will put on; not the life more is than the food and the body [than] the clothing?
pieces: That is why I tell you not to worry about your life, about what you will eat, or about your body, about what you will wear. Is life not more than food, and the body more than clothes?

L.25: Therefore I tell you, do not be anxious about your life, what you will eat, nor about your body, what you will put on. Is not life more than food, and the body [more] than clothing?

R.25: So I tell you, do not worry about having enough food to stay alive or enough clothes to wear. Your life is more important than food, and your body is more important than clothes.

decisions.choice: be anxious: worry, be troubled in mind
decisions.reason: The verb is about anxiety, not about planning. Jesus does not forbid working for food (the birds still look for theirs) but fretting over it.

decisions.choice: therefore: because you cannot serve both God and money
decisions.reason: Worry over food and clothes is the form that serving money takes for the poor.

decisions.choice: what you will eat, the reading of the SBLGNT
alternatives: what you will eat or what you will drink, the reading of many manuscripts
decisions.reason: Many manuscripts add "or what you will drink" (compare 6:31). The evidence is divided. Reviewers should check it against the apparatus.

decisions.choice: worry (B, R); be anxious (L)
decisions.reason: The verb means to be anxious or troubled. Balanced and Readable use the everyday word.

decisions.choice: a statement instead of a question
alternatives: Is not life more than food?
decisions.reason: The question expects the answer yes; Readable gives the answer.

records.heading: Do not worry

records.source: ἐμβλέψατε εἰς τὰ πετεινὰ τοῦ οὐρανοῦ ὅτι οὐ σπείρουσιν οὐδὲ θερίζουσιν οὐδὲ συνάγουσιν εἰς ἀποθήκας, καὶ ὁ πατὴρ ὑμῶν ὁ οὐράνιος τρέφει αὐτά· οὐχ ὑμεῖς μᾶλλον διαφέρετε αὐτῶν;
records.gloss: Look at the birds of the heaven, that not they sow nor reap nor gather into barns, and the Father of you the heavenly feeds them; not you much are worth more than they?
pieces: Look at the birds in the sky. They do not plant or harvest or store food in barns, and yet your heavenly Father feeds them. Are you not worth far more than they are?

L.26: Look at the birds of the sky: they do not sow or reap or gather into barns, and your heavenly Father feeds them. Are you not worth much more than they?

R.26: Look at the birds. They do not plant seeds or gather crops or store food in barns. But your Father in heaven feeds them. You are worth much more than birds.

decisions.choice: from the lesser to the greater: if God feeds birds, he will care for his children
decisions.reason: The argument runs from the smaller case to the larger, a common Jewish way of reasoning. Birds do not farm, yet God provides; disciples who do work need not fret.

decisions.choice: a statement instead of a question
alternatives: Are you not worth much more?
decisions.reason: As in 6:25.

records.source: τίς δὲ ἐξ ὑμῶν μεριμνῶν δύναται προσθεῖναι ἐπὶ τὴν ἡλικίαν αὐτοῦ πῆχυν ἕνα;
records.gloss: Who but of you being anxious is able to add to the span of life of him cubit one?
pieces: Can any of you add a single hour to your life by worrying?

L.27: And which of you by being anxious can add one cubit to {{gender:their|his}} span of life?

R.27: You cannot add even one hour to your life by worrying about it.

decisions.choice: add a cubit to the span of life: lengthen life even a little
alternatives: add a cubit to one's height
decisions.reason: The word can mean length of life or stature, and a cubit is a measure of about eighteen inches. Adding a cubit to one's height would be no small thing, so a little more life is the likelier sense: worry cannot add even a moment.

decisions.choice: a single hour
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable turn the picture of a measure into one of time, as the meaning note explains. Literal keeps "cubit".

decisions.choice: worry (B, R); be anxious (L)
decisions.reason: The verb means to be anxious or troubled. Balanced and Readable use the everyday word.

records.source: καὶ περὶ ἐνδύματος τί μεριμνᾶτε;
records.gloss: And about clothing why are you anxious?
pieces: And why do you worry about clothes?

L.28: And why are you anxious about clothing?

R.28: And why do you worry about clothes?

decisions.choice: worry (B, R); be anxious (L)
decisions.reason: The verb means to be anxious or troubled. Balanced and Readable use the everyday word.

records.source: καταμάθετε τὰ κρίνα τοῦ ἀγροῦ πῶς αὐξάνουσιν· οὐ κοπιῶσιν οὐδὲ νήθουσιν·
records.gloss: Consider the lilies of the field how they grow; not they labor nor spin;
pieces: Think about how the wildflowers grow. They neither toil nor spin thread.

L.28: Consider the lilies of the field, how they grow: they do not labor or spin,

R.28: Look at how the wildflowers in the fields grow. They do not work or make clothes for themselves.

decisions.choice: the lilies of the field: wild flowers in general
decisions.reason: The word names lilies, but in this setting it covers the bright flowers of Galilee's hillsides, which grow wild.

decisions.choice: labor, spin: the work of men in the fields and of women making cloth
decisions.reason: The birds do not do men's work (6:26); the flowers do not do women's work.

decisions.choice: wildflowers
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable name what is meant; Literal keeps "lilies".

records.source: λέγω δὲ ὑμῖν ὅτι οὐδὲ Σολομὼν ἐν πάσῃ τῇ δόξῃ αὐτοῦ περιεβάλετο ὡς ἓν τούτων.
records.gloss: I say but to you that not even Solomon in all the glory of him was clothed as one of these.
pieces: But I tell you, Solomon in all his glory was never dressed as beautifully as one of them.

L.29: But I tell you that not even Solomon in all his glory was clothed like one of these.

R.29: But I tell you, even King Solomon with all his riches and glory did not have clothes as beautiful as these flowers.

decisions.choice: Solomon in all his glory: Israel's richest king
decisions.reason: Solomon's wealth and splendor were famous (1 Kings 10:4-7, 23).

records.source: εἰ δὲ τὸν χόρτον τοῦ ἀγροῦ σήμερον ὄντα καὶ αὔριον εἰς κλίβανον βαλλόμενον ὁ θεὸς οὕτως ἀμφιέννυσιν, οὐ πολλῷ μᾶλλον ὑμᾶς, ὀλιγόπιστοι;
records.gloss: If but the grass of the field today being and tomorrow into an oven being thrown the God thus clothes, not much more you, little-faiths?
pieces: If that is how God clothes the wild grass, which is here today and thrown into the oven tomorrow, will {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} not clothe you much more, you who have so little faith?

L.30: But if God so clothes the grass of the field, which is [here] today and tomorrow is thrown into an oven, [will {{deity_pronoun:he|He}}] not much more [clothe] you, you of little faith?

R.30: God dresses the grass in the fields like that. The grass is there today, and tomorrow it is burned in an oven. So God will surely give you clothes. Your faith is so small!

decisions.choice: thrown into an oven: dried grass was used as fuel
decisions.reason: Wood was scarce, and dried grass and weeds fired the clay ovens used for baking.

decisions.choice: you of little faith: people who trust God too little
decisions.reason: Matthew uses this word for the disciples when their trust gives way (8:26; 14:31; 16:8). It is a rebuke to believers.

decisions.choice: a statement instead of a question
alternatives: will he not much more clothe you?
decisions.reason: As in 6:25.

records.source: μὴ οὖν μεριμνήσητε λέγοντες· Τί φάγωμεν;
records.gloss: Not therefore be anxious saying, What shall we eat?
pieces: So do not worry and say, 'What will we eat?'

L.31: So do not be anxious, saying, 'What shall we eat?'

R.31: So do not worry and say, 'What will we eat?'

decisions.choice: worry (B, R); be anxious (L)
decisions.reason: The verb means to be anxious or troubled. Balanced and Readable use the everyday word.

records.source: ἤ· Τί πίωμεν;
records.gloss: Or, What shall we drink?
pieces: or, 'What will we drink?'

decisions.choice: the second of three anxious questions
decisions.reason: The SBLGNT marks each question as its own sentence. Together they repeat the worries of 6:25.

records.source: ἤ· Τί περιβαλώμεθα;
records.gloss: Or, What shall we put on?
pieces: or, 'What will we wear?'

decisions.choice: the third of the anxious questions
decisions.reason: As in the previous sentence.

records.source: πάντα γὰρ ταῦτα τὰ ἔθνη ἐπιζητοῦσιν· οἶδεν γὰρ ὁ πατὴρ ὑμῶν ὁ οὐράνιος ὅτι χρῄζετε τούτων ἁπάντων.
records.gloss: All for these things the Gentiles seek after; knows for the Father of you the heavenly that you need these all.
pieces: The pagans chase after all these things, and your heavenly Father knows that you need them all.

L.32: For the Gentiles seek after all these things; for your heavenly Father knows that you need them all.

R.32: People who do not know God are always trying to get these things. But your Father in heaven knows that you need them.

decisions.choice: the Gentiles: people who do not know the God of Israel
decisions.reason: As in 6:7. Those who have no Father in heaven to trust must strive for these things on their own.

decisions.choice: people who do not know God
decisions.reason: As in 5:47.

records.source: ζητεῖτε δὲ πρῶτον τὴν βασιλείαν καὶ τὴν δικαιοσύνην αὐτοῦ, καὶ ταῦτα πάντα προστεθήσεται ὑμῖν.
records.gloss: Seek but first the kingdom and the righteousness of him, and these things all will be added to you.
pieces: Above all, seek the kingdom and {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} righteousness, and you will be given all these things as well.

L.33: But seek first the kingdom and {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} righteousness, and all these things will be added to you.

R.33: Above everything else, look for God's kingdom and do what is righteous in {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} eyes. Then God will give you all these other things too.

decisions.choice: his righteousness: the right living God requires, and God's justice
alternatives: the righteousness God credits to believers
decisions.reason: As throughout the sermon (5:6, 20; 6:1), righteousness is doing God's will. "His" is the Father of 6:32.

decisions.choice: the kingdom and his righteousness, the reading of the SBLGNT
alternatives: the kingdom of God and his righteousness, the reading of many manuscripts
decisions.reason: Many manuscripts read "the kingdom of God". The meaning is the same. Reviewers should check the evidence against the apparatus.

decisions.choice: will be added: God will give them
decisions.reason: The passive points to God, as often in Jesus's sayings (5:4).

decisions.choice: God's kingdom; God will give you
decisions.reason: Readable names God.

records.source: μὴ οὖν μεριμνήσητε εἰς τὴν αὔριον, ἡ γὰρ αὔριον μεριμνήσει αὑτῆς· ἀρκετὸν τῇ ἡμέρᾳ ἡ κακία αὐτῆς.
records.gloss: Not therefore be anxious for the tomorrow, the for tomorrow will be anxious of itself; sufficient to the day the trouble of it.
pieces: So do not be troubled about tomorrow; tomorrow can take care of its own worries. Today's trouble is enough for today.

L.34: So do not be anxious about tomorrow, for tomorrow will be anxious about itself; sufficient for the day [is] its own trouble.

R.34: So do not worry about tomorrow. Tomorrow will have its own worries. Each day has enough trouble in it.

decisions.choice: tomorrow will be anxious about itself: take each day's troubles as they come
decisions.reason: The saying is a proverb. It does not promise an easy tomorrow; it forbids carrying tomorrow's load today.
